concepts.why: The presence of a focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion along the anterosuperior wall of the urinary bladder and a well-defined soft-tissue–density lesion with calcific specks supports this diagnosis.
The symptoms of dysuria and hematuria, along with the presence of red blood cells and pus cells in the urinalysis, suggest a urinary tract infection.
The patient's history of abdominal hysterectomy and the presence of a cystic area in the left adnexa and left hydrosalpinx support the possibility of endometriosis.
The presence of a right calyceal calculus with mild pelvicalyceal dilatation supports the diagnosis of a kidney stone.
The indistinct outline of the adjacent bladder wall and heterogeneous enhancement in the early arterial and venous phases suggest a granulomatous lesion.
The presence of a focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion and a well-defined soft-tissue–density lesion with calcific specks along the anterosuperior bladder wall could also suggest bladder cancer.
The presence of left hydrosalpinx is a distinct finding that supports this diagnosis.
The presence of a simple right renal cyst is a distinct finding that supports this diagnosis.
The symptoms of dysuria and the presence of left hydrosalpinx support the possibility of pelvic inflammatory disease.
The chronic nature of the symptoms of dysuria and hematuria, along with the presence of red blood cells and pus cells in the urinalysis, suggest chronic cystitis.

rationales.F11: The presence of a right calyceal calculus with mild pelvicalyceal dilatation is highly suggestive of a kidney stone.
rationales.F12: The presence of a left hydrosalpinx is highly suggestive of a condition such as endometriosis or pelvic inflammatory disease.
